summary: Palette-indexed texture color conversion writing one RGB row. Reads three source byte streams from the a2 pointer array at byte offset 4*a3, indexes four lookup tables by pairs of bytes from those streams, and writes 3 output bytes per pixel (no alpha). The main loop converts two pixels per iteration and runs a1[23] >> 1 times; when the row width is odd one trailing pixel is written. Every output channel is byte(source + tableValue + base) with the middle channel combining two tables via a >> 16 blend.

operations.description: Load the palette LUT sub-object v4 from this->+0x19C (a1[103]); its entries v4[4..7] hold the four lookup tables.
Read the additive base from this->+0x11C (a1[71]) and the row width from this->+0x5C (a1[23]).
Read the four lookup-table pointers from v4[4] (+0x1AC), v4[5] (+0x1B0), v4[6] (+0x1B4) and v4[7] (+0x1B8).
Resolve three source streams a2[0..2] at byte offset 4*a3 and take the destination row pointer from *a4.
When a1[23] >> 1 is zero the two-pixel loop is skipped entirely.
Two-pixel-per-iteration loop running a1[23] >> 1 times, consuming two bytes of each source stream per iteration.
Index the four tables by bytes from the second and third source streams; the middle channel sums two table values and shifts the sum >> 16.
Write 6 output bytes per iteration (two RGB pixels), each channel computed as byte(source byte + table value + base).
When the row width is odd (a1[23] & 1), process one trailing pixel after the loop.
Write the final 3 output bytes for the odd trailing pixel using the same table lookups and base addition.
Return the destination pointer at the end of the written row.
